correctness.rationale: Exact Parseval on powers of the same prime gives the single-circle zeta trace. Completing the square provides a nonnegative boundary gap with one quadratic contact, one quartic contact, or two quadratic contacts. The Laurent pole of zeta has uniformly bounded remainder; local quadratic/quartic scaling yields all fixed-parameter constants. For b=a/4-kappa sqrt(delta), a delta^(1/4) angular rescaling and a uniform quartic-tail domination give an exact rational-integral limit and its closed form. The supplementary checker passed 83 finite symbolic and numerical assertions; it is not a proof of infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The new statement is an exact sharp Hilbert–Schmidt mass and detuning crossover for the correlated one-prime two-harmonic family. Bayart–Brevig (2015) already treat quartic boundary contact and its compactness implications, which are expressly excluded from the originality claim. Bayart–Kouroupis (2023) supply general Schatten criteria, not the exact single-circle zeta-integral and two-parameter crossover. The two closest published calculations are independent-prime Bessel S2 and independent-prime S4 traces with nonidentical Gram structure. No direct coverage was located in the inspected material; residual historical-priority risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: In a canonical Hardy–Dirichlet composition family, correlated prime powers generate a tunable transition from one to two boundary contact points. Near coalescence, the Hilbert–Schmidt mass has a different, faster divergence exponent and a nontrivial universal-scale unfolding that cannot be recovered by naively taking fixed-side limits. This provides quantitative sensitivity of singular-value energy to perturbations at a known contact-type bifurcation and distinguishes it from independent-prime Bessel thresholds. The precise constants and crossover are natural spectral invariants, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
